title: WTF do people use Open Models for??
talk_summary: A usage-data talk from Featherless AI's CEO about what people actually run on open models: creative/roleplay dominates, coding agents are 20-30% of traffic and token-hungry, and enterprise users prize model stability over benchmark chasing. The actionable core is a reliability-engineering argument: ship 80-90% automation with human escape hatches, iterate on failure slices, and pin model versions instead of swapping weekly.

takeaways.technique: Human escape hatches / 80% automation with review gate
takeaways.what_they_do: Build agents that draft 80-90% of work but route every output through a human (or reviewer) for final approval, then incrementally auto-approve only proven-reliable classes.
takeaways.numbers: 80-90% auto-drafted, humans handle remainder; teams going 100% automation got burned

takeaways.technique: Pin model versions; don't chase weekly model swaps
takeaways.what_they_do: Production users stick to a fixed model version because prompt-tuned 99%+ accuracy breaks when the provider updates the model; they only change deliberately.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they really do not want to change their system and have it break overnight ... use a stable model version in open source and ... not change the model because if it end broke don't fix it
takeaways.numbers: Mistral Nemo still dominant 8 months after being superseded; Llama 2 ~2% of workload

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of chasing 100% automation, solve 80-90% of scenarios reliably, then take the remaining 10-20% failure slice and solve 80-90% of that, repeating to compound reliability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: do it for another 80 to 90% for that 10 to 20% failure scenarios and repeat this process 10 times and now suddenly you have 99.998% reliability

takeaways.technique: Small models are 'good enough' for high-volume subtasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Autocomplete-class coding is served by 3B-12B models because it's effectively solved; small models are far cheaper at scale and four small models cost the same as one big one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these features are now being served by dozens of AI model that are small and arguably good enough with parameter size ranging from 3 billion to 12 billion
takeaways.numbers: 3B-12B params; 4 small models ≈ price of 1 big model

takeaways.technique: Ship to production early, iterate from real usage
takeaways.what_they_do: Teams that build the whole automated workflow before production get burned; the advice is to get a partial system into real use fast and integrate/iterate from there.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your goal is to go beyond the PC phase and in to adoption in your company at scale in some portion as fast as possible and to inter uh integrate and iterate from there

takeaways.technique: Don't rely on benchmarks; measure task-level reliability
takeaways.what_they_do: Benchmarks have lost meaning; what matters is whether an agent can be trusted to do one instructed task without hallucination or failure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how many of our AI agents today can be reliably be trusted with one task it's instructed to do so without hallucination or failure
